title: From ARM64 to x86-64
description:
GCC compiled four C functions for **ARM64**. Read them, work out what they do, and write the same functions for x86-64.

ARM64 reminders: arguments arrive in `x0`, `x1`, `x2`, and the result goes back in `x0`. Instructions have three operands: `sub x0, x0, x2` means x0 = x0 − x2. `ldr x3, [x2], 8` loads the 8 bytes at x2 into x3, then adds 8 to x2. `lsl 3` and `lsr 63` shift an operand left by 3 or right by 63 on the way in. `csel x0, x1, x0, ge` picks x1 if the last comparison said "greater or equal", otherwise x0; `csneg x0, x0, x0, ge` picks x0 if "greater or equal", otherwise its negation.

```
mystery1:
        mul     x0, x0, x1
        sub     x0, x0, x2
        ret

mystery2:
        cmp     x0, 0
        csneg   x0, x0, x0, ge
        ret

mystery3:
        cmp     x1, 0
        ble     .L8
        mov     x2, x0
        add     x1, x0, x1, lsl 3
        mov     x0, 0
.L7:
        ldr     x3, [x2], 8
        add     x0, x0, x3, lsr 63
        cmp     x1, x2
        bne     .L7
        ret
.L8:
        mov     x0, 0
        ret

mystery5:
        cmp     x1, x0
        csel    x0, x1, x0, ge
        ret
```

starter.solution.asm:
mystery1:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

mystery2:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

mystery3:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

mystery5:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
mystery1:                               ; a * b - c
        mov     rax, rdi
        imul    rax, rsi
        sub     rax, rdx
        ret

mystery2:                               ; the absolute value
        mov     rax, rdi
        neg     rax
        cmovs   rax, rdi
        ret

mystery3:                               ; how many of the n numbers are negative
        xor     eax, eax
        lea     rdx, [rdi + rsi*8]
.loop:  cmp     rdi, rdx
        jae     .done
        mov     rcx, [rdi]
        shr     rcx, 63                 ; the sign bit: 1 for a negative number
        add     rax, rcx
        add     rdi, 8
        jmp     .loop
.done:  ret

mystery5:                               ; the larger of the two
        mov     rax, rdi
        cmp     rsi, rdi
        cmovge  rax, rsi
        ret

hints: In `mystery3`, `x3, lsr 63` is the loaded number shifted right by 63: just its sign bit. Adding that up counts something.
unitTests:
test "mystery1"
    mystery1(6, 7, 2) == 40
    mystery1(-3, 4, 0) == -12
    mystery1(0, 99, 5) == -5
test "mystery2"
    mystery2(-8) == 8
    mystery2(8) == 8
    mystery2(0) == 0
test "mystery3"
    mystery3([1, -2, 3, -4, -5], 5) == 3
    mystery3([1, 2, 3], 3) == 0
    mystery3([-1], 0) == 0
test "mystery5"
    mystery5(3, 9) == 9
    mystery5(9, 3) == 9
    mystery5(-4, -4) == -4
